title: JSON Web Token (JWT)
subtitle: Scoped JWTs for agent seats, employee-scoped tokens for Microsoft identities, bearer introspection that fails closed. Identity in my systems is derived from the token, never from tool input.

stats.label: each issuer's key set is cached at the gateway
runtimes trusting the same kind of anchor

lede: In the Auth and access plane I had assistants from several vendors calling one private tool estate, and I wanted every call checked without a round trip to the issuer. I made JWTs the token format and published keys the trust anchor. My Python OAuth server issues RS256-signed access tokens carrying issuer, audience, expiry and coarse MCP scope claims, publishes its key set and persists its signing key, so assistants holding long-lived refresh tokens keep working through a restart. The Rust tool gateway validates against published key sets from more than one issuer, which lets it accept tokens from my server and from Microsoft's platform.
quote: A caller cannot name itself in the arguments.
evidence: OAuth and identity architecture: RS256 tokens issued in Python and checked offline in Rust and at the edge against published key sets cached for 1 hour.
Delegation security for AI agents: every agent-to-agent message a signed JWT over a canonical hash, with depth limits and cycle detection.
Least privilege for AI agents: identity derived from the token on every surface, never from tool arguments, and a sub-agent's identity ends with its parent's.
author: Corey James
